The installers' own `--help` text, and the options and environment variables it lists.

## install.sh (users)

The user installer at the repo root. Piped from `curl`, or `./install.sh` from a clone.

```text
Install AI Task Tracking on this Mac (macOS 13+, Apple Silicon or Intel). Re-running it upgrades: the app is
quit and replaced, and reopened only if it was running; your data folder and settings stay.

  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/altoption/ai-task-tracking/HEAD/install.sh | bash
  … | bash -s -- [options]       (options when piped)
  ./install.sh [options]         (from a clone: builds that checkout when no release is used)

It checks what this Mac has, shows what it will do, and asks once. Then it installs the latest notarized
release (or builds from source when there is none, it fails verification, or --from-source; Bun is then
installed if missing), links ~/.local/bin/aitt, runs `aitt setup` and, on a first install, opens the app.

Options:
  --yes             don't ask; take the defaults
  --dry-run         only show what was found and what would happen
  --from-source     build from source even when a release is available
  --version <tag>   that release (or source tag) instead of the latest, e.g. v0.2.0
  --no-launch       don't open the app, at the end or after a failure
  --connect <tools> connect these other agent tools (comma-separated, as in aitt setup --connect); a scratch
                    install connects none otherwise
Environment:
  AITT_HOME=<dir>     data folder (default: the one the app already uses, else asked; ~/AITaskTracking)
  AITT_APP_DIR=<dir>  where the app goes (default ~/Applications). A folder other than ~/Applications or
                      /Applications is a scratch install: not registered with macOS, no app settings written,
                      no Claude Code MCP entry, no aitt link and no other agent tools (unless --connect).
```

### Options

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--yes` | don't ask; take the defaults |
| `--dry-run` | only show what was found and what would happen |
| `--from-source` | build from source even when a release is available |
| `--version <tag>` | that release (or source tag) instead of the latest, e.g. v0.2.0 |
| `--no-launch` | don't open the app, at the end or after a failure |
| `--connect <tools>` | connect these other agent tools (comma-separated, as in aitt setup --connect); a scratch install connects none otherwise |

### Environment

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AITT_HOME=<dir>` | data folder (default: the one the app already uses, else asked; ~/AITaskTracking) |
| `AITT_APP_DIR=<dir>` | where the app goes (default ~/Applications). A folder other than ~/Applications or /Applications is a scratch install: not registered with macOS, no app settings written, no Claude Code MCP entry, no aitt link and no other agent tools (unless --connect). |

## uninstall.sh (users)

The user uninstaller at the repo root. It runs `aitt uninstall` from the installed app.

```text
Uninstall AI Task Tracking from this Mac. Your data folder is kept (the output says where it is).

  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/altoption/ai-task-tracking/HEAD/uninstall.sh | bash
  … | bash -s -- --yes              (options when piped)
  ./uninstall.sh [--yes]            (from a clone)

Runs `aitt uninstall` from the installed app: it quits the app, then removes the app, its login item, and the MCP
entries (Claude Code and other agent tools) and ~/.local/bin/aitt link that run this app; also the agent skill and
the CLAUDE.md line, unless another install stays registered. It asks first; --yes doesn't.

Environment: AITT_APP_DIR=<dir>  where the app is installed (default ~/Applications, then /Applications)
```

## scripts/install.sh (developers)

The developer installer: rebuilds this checkout into the app folder.

```text
Usage: scripts/install.sh [--connect <tools>]
Developer installer: build the engine (UI embedded) and "AI Task Tracking.app" from this checkout, install it,
register the MCP server, put `aitt` on PATH and open the app.
Users run ./install.sh at the repo root instead (prebuilt release, or a build through the same functions).

  --connect <tools>   connect these other agent tools (comma-separated, as in aitt setup --connect);
                      without it, no other agent tool is connected or changed
  -h, --help          show this and exit

Environment:
  AITT_HOME=<dir>      data folder the app runs the engine on (default: the folder the app already uses,
                       else ~/AITaskTracking); remembered by the app
  AITT_APP_DIR=<dir>   where the app is installed (default ~/Applications). Any folder other than
                       ~/Applications or /Applications is a scratch install: no Launch Services registration, no
                       app settings, no Claude Code MCP entry, no aitt link and no other agent tools (unless
                       --connect names them).
  SKIP_MCP=1           don't register the user-scope `ai-task-tracking` MCP entry or link `aitt`
  SKIP_LOGIN_ITEM=1    don't turn on Launch at Login (otherwise every run turns it on; harmless when already on)
  NO_LAUNCH=1          don't open the app at the end
```

### Options

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--connect <tools>` | connect these other agent tools (comma-separated, as in aitt setup --connect); without it, no other agent tool is connected or changed |
| `-h, --help` | show this and exit |

### Environment

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AITT_HOME=<dir>` | data folder the app runs the engine on (default: the folder the app already uses, else ~/AITaskTracking); remembered by the app |
| `AITT_APP_DIR=<dir>` | where the app is installed (default ~/Applications). Any folder other than ~/Applications or /Applications is a scratch install: no Launch Services registration, no app settings, no Claude Code MCP entry, no aitt link and no other agent tools (unless --connect names them). |
| `SKIP_MCP=1` | don't register the user-scope `ai-task-tracking` MCP entry or link `aitt` |
| `SKIP_LOGIN_ITEM=1` | don't turn on Launch at Login (otherwise every run turns it on; harmless when already on) |
| `NO_LAUNCH=1` | don't open the app at the end |
